title: Campaign checkpointing & artifact quarantine scheduler for calibration campaigns
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Calibration campaigns (FP8/INT8 sweeps) produce many intermediate artifacts and long-running jobs. Teams need safe checkpointing, temporary quarantining of partial artifacts pending accuracy validation, and predictable garbage collection so storage and compliance SLAs are met.

Goal: Build a scheduler and artifact lifecycle policy surfaced in Redwood Console that: 1) performs periodic campaign checkpointing to enable deterministic shard replay and restartability, 2) quarantines artifacts until an accuracy validation gating step approves promotion, 3) exposes TTL and cold-storage rules per artifact type, and 4) enforces RBAC for promotion/restore/GC operations.

Non-goals: This ticket is not implementing new quantization algorithms or the accuracy validator models themselves; it is focused on orchestration, metadata, and UX for artifact lifecycle and campaign checkpointing.

Constraints & considerations:
- Checkpoints must be small metadata manifests plus referenced blob pointers (not full model copies) to keep storage costs low.
- Some customers require immutable WORM-like retention windows; policy design must accommodate both ephemeral and compliance tiers.
- Promotion gating will integrate with existing accuracy-validation webhooks (ENG-28911) but must be robust to transient validator outages.
- Quarantined artifacts should remain discoverable in Console with limited visibility until promoted by an approver role.

Success measures:
- Restart of interrupted campaigns from checkpoints with <5% increase in wall-clock time versus uninterrupted runs.
- Reduction in peak storage usage for long campaigns by 35% through TTL/cold-storage rules.
- >90% of artifact promotions executed via Console RBAC flows without engineer intervention.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI exposes campaign-level checkpoint cadence and TTL settings
Engineers can create 'quarantine' policy that holds artifacts until manual or automated approval
Checkpoint manifests include shard pointers and checksum metadata and can be used to resume a campaign
Promotion workflow respects RBAC: only users with 'artifact_promote' role can move items from quarantine to promoted storage
Automated GC respects per-artifact TTL and cold-storage migration rules
Integration tests that simulate validator outage still allow safe rollback and requeue of promotion jobs
tasks: Design checkpoint manifest schema and minimal metadata payload
Implement scheduler service to emit checkpoints and trigger TTL transitions
Add quarantine state to artifact metadata store and index in search
Console UX: policy editor for checkpoint cadence, quarantine TTL, and approver lists
RBAC: add 'artifact_promote' and 'artifact_restore' roles and map to org/team permissions
Integration: hook promotion step to accuracy validator webhook with retry/backoff
E2E tests: shard replay and restart from checkpoint
Run a pilot campaign with internal quantization team and collect metrics
decisions: Use manifest-based checkpoints (small JSON + blob refs) instead of full model snapshots to save storage and speed restarts
Quarantine is a metadata state, not a separate physical bucket by default; cold-storage migration will be a separate transition
Promotion approvals will first be automated via accuracy webhook; fallback to manual approver in Console if validator is unavailable
TTL default will be 30 days for ephemeral artifacts, configurable per project; compliance tiers will support immutable retention via separate workflow
